title.narrative: Creating Safe Spaces Online for Freedom of Expression

description.narrative: Implemented Activities Within the Period Under Review were building a Digital Rights violations reporting platform, website upgrade, Strategic Litigation, Capacity Building, Digital Rights Workshops, Digital Rights Media Fellowship, Research, Digital Rights in Africa Report, Media and Communication, Digital Rights and Inclusion Forum (2020 and 2021), and participating in global convenings (RightsCon and FOC). Media Fellowship: the Fellowship program is designed to immerse selected journalists in digital rights advocacy and intervention efforts in Africa. The fellows published stories on topics such as digital platforms and protests, digital footprints in policy, language diversity online, hate speech, and fundamental human rights. Digital Rights in Africa Report: The 2019 Digital Rights in Africa report provided in-depth analysis on the state of digital rights in Nigeria and 12 other African countries. It examined violations such as Internet disruptions, illegal surveillance, the arrest of bloggers, and the passage of hurtful legislation. In addition to this, we converted the report into a short movie titled Training Day. By the end of the reporting period, the movie grossed over 360,000 views on YouTube and over 1.1 million on Facebook. The 2020 report, named Londa, echoes the call for the collective work of different stakeholders to protect the digital rights environment in Africa. The report analyses the state of digital rights and inclusion in 20 African countries and makes key recommendations for improving the digital rights landscape. Media and Publicity Engagements : (a) Media Parleys: We held two media parleys(b) Online Advertisements: We created audiovisual content that enabled us to run adverts on all our social media platforms (Youtube, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn). (c) Newspaper Advertisements: We ran newspaper advertisements on the proposed Social Medial bill in Nigeria and also ran advertisements condemning civic restrictions (d) Radio Advertisement: We ran infomercials on 3 radio stations in Abuja for one week towards pushback on the anti-social media bill. We also started a #SayNoToSocialMediaBill radio tour that featured the need for a rights-respecting approach to legislative proposals on radio stations in 26 states. Digital Rights Violation Reporting Platform RIPOTI: RIPOTI, the web platform for reporting digital rights violations has been completed and launched. The platform is being used to report, document, and process human rights violations online. It serves as a platform for collaborative intervention, research, and whistleblowing around state-induced clampdowns against freedom of expression. Digital Rights Toolkit: The Ayeta toolkit was developed with the overarching aim of addressing the need to safeguard digital rights defenders, journalists, whistleblowers, and others working with sensitive information in the global South. Paradigm Initiative (PIN) is dedicated to making the toolkit user-friendly and ensuring it remains a living resource. Capacity Building: We reached 45 civil society organizations in our 3-day workshop held in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, in February 2020. We rescheduled others to 2021 due to the COVID 19 lockdown. Strategic Litigation: For the period under review, we filed court cases in support of wrongfully accused #EndSARS protesters, we issued a joint statement calling for respect for citizens’ rights during protests and challenged the violation of citizens' rights. Global Convenings (RightsCon and Freedom Online Conference) Participation in relevant and strategic global convenings was proposed as part of the project. The objective of our participation is to provide a platform to present our research and advocacy work to a global audience, learn from best practices across the world and benefit from diverse expertise available at such meetings. We have participated in two out of four convenings proposed and we have hosted three side sessions dedicated to our work on these platforms. We will be participating at RightsCon in June 2021 and Freedom Online Conference later in the year. Risks, Challenges and Mitigating Measures: The unprecedented episode of the COVID-19 pandemic caused a major disruption to our work causing activities to be either suspended, cancelled or postponed causing a low rate of depletion for this project. The financial excesses reported for Year 1 are mostly as a result of activities not yet carried out due to the COVID-19 restrictions but are now set to be implemented in Year 2, as indicated in the annual plan. While some project activities were interrupted by the COVID-19 lockdowns, we have not departed from the theory of change as we continued to ensure that online activities helped drive home our message about the need to create safe spaces online. Sustainability: Sustainability in this project will be guaranteed based on the following:. We position ourselves for funding and institutional support by demonstrating leadership in our field. We continue to offer value and engage broadly, bringing attention to our work in relevant circles. Our sustainability plan is built around developing a community of partners and organisations through our Netsrights Coalition. Our work will extend beyond the project lifeline for the following reasons (a) Paradigm Initiative has been active on the Internet Freedom scene in Africa for over 10 years, and has acquired the reputation of impact and have also forged partnerships with organizations within Nigeria, such as the Nigerian Network of NGOs, Digital Rights Lawyers Initiative, Citizens’ Gavel, among others (b) Our Internet freedom interventions across Africa over the past 10 years has involved the train-the-trainer model. This process continues to produce a ripple effect that effectively multiplies our impact and ensures that our work is sustainable even if particular programs have ended. (c) Paradigm Initiative has multiple and diverse long-term funding partners that support our work for the foreseeable future. For example, our 5 year grant relationship with Ford Foundation; our 2-year grant, covering 5 countries, with the United States’ Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor; and our 3-year Greater Internet Freedom project supported by the United States Agency for International Development. Conclusion: We are excited by the level of implementation of this project despite the limitations imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. We are on course to achieve a 100% implementation of the grant and cannot wait to measure the impact of the project on the landscape for freedom of expression online.

The project aims to increase awareness and respect for online freedom of expression by carrying out activities that educate, inform, influence, and support the implementation of policies, laws, and practices on the subject matter. The project is expected to significantly change the overall outlook toward digital engagement in Nigeria.

2 media parleys were held. The first, a physical media parley in Lagos, took place in January 2020 where we discussed the elements of the project with the media. The second parley couldn't hold physically because of Covid-19 imposed restriction. It was held virtually. We also committed funds of 3,406,494 to radio tour accross states in the country.

Ayeta serves as a digital security toolkit and has played a role in educating people, especially in times of rampant internet shutdowns in the past few years. Ayeta toolkit has a download count record of three hundred and four downloads (304).

DRIF21 The event was hosted virtually and in- person in 10 countries, mainly Cameroon, Chad, Namibia, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia. About 445 attendees participated in DRIF21 across 42 countries in Africa and beyond, offering an interactive platform for engaging in robust conversations on digital rights and inclusion in Africa.
There were also impactful discussions on digital health for children, artificial intelligence, digital identity, digital security, building networks, and communities of practice in digital rights
DRIF22 was a hybrid event which featured 13 virtual events in person sessions hosted in 17 African countries featuring organisations, activists, academia, legislature and policymakers within the digital ecosystem. During DRIF22, discussions and debates were focused on issues plaguing the digital sphere in Africa including: data privacy, affordable internet, gender and ICTs, disability rights and ICT health surveillance during COVID-19 times and Internet shutdowns.
The event had 1,042 mentions from Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, and the Web had over 2 million impressions (likes, comments, and shares). Over the two months of the forum, we had a total of 5000+ views on YouTube and 103 new subscribers.

For three years in a row now, we have produced short films derived from our annual Digital Rights and Inclusion Report known as Londa. Londa is a zulu word which is a call to action to protect or defend the digital rights and inclusion environment in Africa.
We converted the reports into film scripts and produced short movies. In 2020 we released Training Day, and in 2021 we converted the report into another short film, Focus. Finding Diana, which is the third short film drawn from the report was released in 2022.
By using visuals and storytelling, PIN has been able to break down complex information into more easily digestible chunks, and this has especially been helpful for our young audience who are not experts in the subject matter of the reports. Training Day features the story of a young man whose quest for work took an unexpected turn. The movie won two Pitcher Awards in 2021 (Silver- Non-Profit Organisations and Bronze- Entertainment Film).
Focus spotlights key issues plaguing the digital rights and inclusion ecosystems. It won three Pitcher Awards in 2022 (Silver-Entertainment Film, Bronze- Film Craft Bronze- Good Category.
Finding Diana follows Aisha as she investigates a story of debauchery in her state government. The movie won an award at the Berlin Short Films Festival in 2023 where it was named the Best Human Rights Film. It also won Pitcher Awards 2023 (Gold Good Category-Non-Profit and Silver-Entertainment Film).
Total number of viewership is 2,870,843
We further organised a series of half-day convenings dubbed ‘Digi-talks with Focus’ in 10 countries. The Convening consisted of a screening of Focus, presentation of Londa country findings, and a panel discussion on the issues and recommendations.
The convenings gathered a diverse target audience of up to 35 participants of PIN and local partners.

The 8th edition of DRIF21 hosted over 30 sessions and provided an unusual opportunity for multi-stakeholder conversation on the issues and post-forum collaborations among stakeholders to speak with one voice and convince African governments on policies around freedom of expression online.
DRIF21 had an exciting agenda with sessions unpacking digital inclusion for marginalized communities, innovations in assistive technologies for persons with disabilities, strategies for tackling internet disruptions in Africa, and the promotion of media freedom through litigation and advocacy.
The 9th edition of DRIF themed ”Towards a Digitally Inclusive Africa” DRIF22 was a hybrid event. The virtual sessions were hosted on Whova platform and 511 attendees registered for the event. The In-person events had 876 attendees from 17 African countries (Namibia,Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Central AfricanRepublic (CAR), Cameroon, Senegal, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, The Gambia, Nigeria,Somalia, and Ghana.). Communications (Online Advertisement, Newspaper Advertisement, Radio Advertisement and Media Parley)

description.narrative:
We conducted two impactful media parleys: one focused on the state of freedom of expression in Nigeria and NITDA's code of practice, while the other marked the launch of the Londa report. In addition, our campaign utilized online advertisements, harnessing audiovisual content for widespread promotion across diverse social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn. We extended our reach further through newspaper advertisements, addressing critical issues such as the proposed Social Media bill and advocating against civic restrictions.
Expanding our campaign to radio, we strategically aired informative segments on three prominent Abuja radio stations for a week, rallying support against the anti-social media bill. Moreover, we initiated a dynamic #SayNoToSocialMediaBill radio tour, engaging with audiences across 26 states to emphasize the importance of an approach that respects individual rights when considering legislative proposals. These comprehensive efforts synergistically conveyed our messages and galvanized public support for our cause.

We also instituted cases after Twitter was banned in Nigeria in the ECOWAS and Local courts. Some of the cases for reference are: PIN vs AGF, NBC, FGN. Suit number: FHC/ABJ/CS/493/2021 at the Federal High Court in Abuja. EiE, PIN & MRA vs MTN, Airtel, Globacom & 9Mobile. Suit Number: FHC/L/CS/954/2021

We instituted a total of 15 cases most of which are are still pending in court
The matter filed at the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice: MRA, PIN, PTC, IPC, TICD & journalists -David Hundeyin, Samuel Ogundipe, Blessing Oladunjoye, and Nwakamri Apollo.vs Federal Republic of Nigeria. Suit number: ECW/CCJ/APP/29/21 . The court held that the ban was illegal and an affront to the right to freedom of expression.
